result.title: Geometry-Aware Time Reparameterization for Flow-Map Distillation
result.summary: Flow-map distillation enables one- and few-step generation by learning finite-time transitions of a pretrained generative ODE. We investigate whether changing the teacher's time parameterization can make these transitions easier to learn. Motivated by the hypothesis that trajectory segments with large normal acceleration are harder to distill, we propose a geometry-aware time reparameterization that allocates more student time to these regions while preserving the teacher's geometric paths and terminal distribution. We derive a shared clock that equalizes a population normal-acceleration statistic under suitable assumptions, and construct a practical approximation from robust, regularized estimates across teacher trajectories. We incorporate this clock into Lagrangian flow-map distillation, using the transformed time coordinate to condition the student. The clock is estimated once before distillation and requires neither teacher retraining nor additional student parameters or inference-time network evaluations. Experiments on synthetic data, CIFAR-10, and CelebA-64 show improved sample quality over identity-time distillation at matched inference budgets, including improvements in one- and two-step image generation. The gains in one-step generation, where no intermediate sampling times can be adjusted, highlight the benefits of time reparameterization during distillation.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究 flow-map 蒸馏，提出按几何（法向加速度）大小重新分配学生模型的时间坐标，使难蒸馏的轨迹段获得更多“学生时间”，并给出可实践的估计方法，在图像生成任务上提升了少步生成质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其时间重参数化、按路径曲率分配计算量的思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 轨迹训练监督、动态计算分配与停止/步数决策提供借鉴线索，但需核查与多模态推理状态更新的实际关联。
